A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FluidGym and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be matched despite additions and renumbering. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original PPO/SAC experiments, D-MPC cylinder-control results, policy-transfer evaluations, runtime measurements, and numerical validation in Section 4 and Appendices B/E.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds DPC, TD-MPC, and PD-controller evaluations, harder 3D airfoil results, algorithm runtime comparisons, and a network-size ablation.

M1.justification: Appendix D.3 replaces v1's D-MPC action-sequence optimization at inference time with an adapted DPC policy that maps observations to actions and learns through differentiable rollouts with gradient clipping. This substantially changes the gradient-control procedure, rather than merely renaming it. FluidGym's core solver and interface architecture remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same four environment classes and 13 configurations remain. Policy training and control evaluation expand from easy Airfoil3D to medium and hard conditions at Reynolds numbers 3000 and 5000, with restricted algorithm participation. These configurations were already defined and runtime-profiled in v1; v2 adds their learned-control evaluation.

E2.justification: V2 replaces D-MPC with DPC in CylinderJet2D comparisons, adds TD-MPC to CylinderJet2D and CylinderRot2D, and adds DPC, TD-MPC, and a classical PD controller to RBC2D. These additions are verified in Tables 9–10 and Appendix E plots. PPO/SAC variants and TCF opposition control remain.

E3.justification: The gradient-controller evaluation changes from test-time D-MPC optimization to DPC policy training and testing, including 40-step rollouts and stopping easy-cylinder training at 10,000 instead of 50,000 steps. V2 also introduces PPO capacity controls, algorithm-level training-time comparisons, and a 10,000-step budget for the newly evaluated hard Airfoil3D case. The stated cylinder reward changes, but the PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.5 compares PPO policy/value networks with widths [64,64] and [256,256] on two tasks, testing whether capacity explains performance. Section 4.6 adds analysis of computational cost versus sample efficiency. Qualitative controller comparisons expand, while the existing grid-refinement, dimensional-transfer, and domain-transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Reported replication increases from three to five seeds for 3D cylinder and easy 3D airfoil experiments. However, v2 Figure 33 specifies four seeds for hard Airfoil3D despite the general five-seed statement and Table 8. IQM reporting and the existing 95% confidence intervals with 2,000 bootstrap replications remain.

E6.justification: Substantial controller results and harder-airfoil outcomes are added, D-MPC results are replaced, and 3D cylinder estimates and aggregate profiles change. For example, RBC2D-easy's best listed heat-transfer improvement changes from MA-PPO's 20.015% in v1 Table 9 to TD-MPC's 31.650% in v2 Table 10; the MA-PPO entry is unchanged. Revised 3D estimates involve increased seed counts and should not be interpreted as same-setting algorithm improvements.

T1.justification: The cylinder reward definition changes from penalizing mean absolute lift to penalizing absolute mean lift in Section 3.2 and Appendix C. These expressions are mathematically inequivalent. The MDP definitions, governing equations, and solver mathematics otherwise remain essentially unchanged, with no new theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the empirical contribution from PPO/SAC to include DPC and TD-MPC, and the conclusion now cites learned DPC control. The introduction narrows coverage wording from all environments to all core environment classes. The central standalone, differentiable, multi-agent, 3D benchmark claim remains.

C2.justification: V2 interprets gradient-based policy learning through sample efficiency and explains its additional runtime through simulator backpropagation. It discloses DPC training degradation and limits demonstrated applicability to CylinderJet2D/RBC2D, shifting future work toward 3D gradient-based learning. Existing transfer interpretations and most practical limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds substantial numerical documentation: mesh construction, resolutions, actuation periods, timesteps, CFL conditions, smoothing parameters, temperature limits, and observation windows. Appendix D newly specifies PPO/SAC layer widths, multi-agent implementation details, DPC settings, and a TD-MPC hyperparameter table. These disclosures materially improve reproducibility without establishing that previously unspecified settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds BEACON to Table 1 and discusses its standalone but nondifferentiable 2D scope. It adds positioning against MuJoCo, credits Beintema's pioneering RBC control work, and cites TD-MPC, advanced continuous-control methods, and PD control. The main novelty positioning remains; the Gym-TORAX publication update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the gradient-control discussion, separates multi-agent interaction into its own subsection, and adds runtime, numerical-setup, and ablation subsections. It also makes local terminology, indexing, affiliation, and publication-header edits. The overall narrative and main section structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds mesh diagrams, an algorithm-runtime figure, and the network-size ablation figure; expands Figure 5 with training curves; and enlarges several result displays. Appendix flow visualizations gain colorbars and informative captions and are rearranged more compactly. Table 4 gains timing columns, hyperparameter tables expand, and runtime-table column ordering is corrected.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the benchmark's differentiability through policy-learning experiments and broader classical/model-based comparisons, beyond v1's online gradient-control demonstration. The capacity check, runtime tradeoff analysis, and extensive numerical documentation improve the credibility and reproducibility of the benchmark. Stale airfoil-exclusion text, inconsistent hard-airfoil seed counts, and the unexplained printed DPC learning rate remain weaknesses, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
